newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's M1 down 1.3 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Israel's M1 down 1.3 pct in March.

text.p: Israel's M1 money supply fell 1.3 percent in March to 17.81 billion shekels following a sharp rise of 2.7 percent in February, the Bank of Israel said on Thursday.
M1 rose by 3.5 percent in March 1996.
In the first-quarter of the year M1 expanded 4.8 percent against 4.3 percent in the year earlier period. In all of 1996 M1 rose 11.9 percent.
Total credit grew 0.6 percent in March to 258.9 billion shekels following a 0.3 percent rise in February and a 1.2 percent increase in March 1996.
In the first-quarter credit rose 2.1 percent.
Money supply is one of the factors the Bank of Israel uses to determine interest rates. The central bank will announce its May monetary programme later this month.
